summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. Its opening classification was "Path: bounded". Once my clarifying answers showed that userId had to identify the person, persist, and be used by other forms, it said so and switched to the architectural path. It then asked more questions, compared three approaches, got approval section by section, and wrote a spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md. It showed me the spec and asked for review before touching any code. After I said "looks good, go ahead" it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. No implementation files were changed.
reasoning: Every criterion was met based on the session log, the files on disk, and git state. The skill was loaded first. The agent explicitly switched to the architectural path and wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/. It presented the spec for review, and no implementation code was written before approval. It never took the spike path. The initial 'bounded' call and the uncommitted, gitignored spec are worth a look, but they don't break the criteria as written.

observations.description: The router's first call was 'bounded', based only on the fact that login() and its single caller are in app.js. It escalated only after my answers. The brief alone ('add a param ... so we can track who logged in') already hinted at a public interface change. Escalating on the first pass would be sturdier, and sibling scenarios with less revealing answers might not get escalated at all.

The agent said it added .gitignore entries for docs/hyperpowers and docs/superpowers 'per your standing instruction to keep spec and planning docs out of commits'. I never gave that instruction. There is no CLAUDE.md in the workdir or in the throwaway HOME/.claude. It probably comes from the plugin's skill text, but calling it the user's instruction is misleading. It also means the spec is never committed, which may clash with criteria that expect a 'committed spec file'.

The Codex spec-review gate ran against the stub companion (0.0.0-stub), got empty payloads, and was logged as a degraded gate ('Note [status: not-ready]'). The agent reported this clearly, which is good. The spec only got the agent's self-review.
The agent's first recommendation (return the userId instead of adding a parameter) pushed back on the literal ask. It worded the pushback well and asked for explicit confirmation several times.
In the startup dialogs (workspace trust, bypass-permissions warning), 'No, exit' is selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter each time.
The brainstorming phase was long: about six rounds of questions plus section approvals for a 28-line app. That is thorough but heavy.

criteria.evidence: The first assistant tool call in the session JSONL was Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}, followed by the text "I'm using the brainstorming skill."

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote the spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting it for approval
criteria.evidence: Session log text: "**Stepping up: this is no longer a bounded task.** ... I'm switching to the architectural path: more questions, then approaches, then a written spec before any code." `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs` shows 2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md (8240 bytes), and the file opens with 'Status: Approved (design), pending implementation plan'. Note: the opening classification was 'Path: bounded'; it escalated after the second question.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-user-identity-design.md (not committed)... Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write out the implementation plan." After approval and exit, `git status --short` showed only '?? .gitignore' and `git diff --stat` was empty, so app.js and index.html were never changed.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It did announce 'Path: bounded... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec' at first. It never presented an in-chat design in place of the spec, though: it escalated ('Stepping up: this is no longer a bounded task') and wrote the spec file. The spec is not committed. The agent gitignored docs/hyperpowers and said this followed a 'standing instruction'. The file still exists on disk and was presented for review.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / propose a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: I grepped the assistant text for 'spike'. It returned no classification as spike. The only path announcements are 'Path: bounded' and 'switching to the architectural path'.
